title: Nine Boxes of Order
subtitle: 类别与分类 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 类别与分类（科学与技术·逻辑与分类）
meta: 主题语境：类别与分类（科学与技术·逻辑与分类）　|　核心词汇：category　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 category 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 my mother was sent to name ① a category she could not fill, and she said the filling was the whole of the lesson. The ② category, meaning the box and not the entries, was nine lines deep and was filled by whoever came last; a category, she said, is the only thing in a table that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ category in that table had the same heading, and the ④ category at the end, meaning the one the clerk kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever named properly. A category, my grandmother said, is nine parts order and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the order is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ category was the whole of the kind, meaning the type it named and not the box. The ⑥ category, meaning the kind and not any of that, is the only thing in a science that everybody uses and nobody questions; a category, he said, is either something you name or the only word that means both a box and a kind. She said the kind is the part they remember.

By 1976 the ⑦ category had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the heading. The ⑧ category of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine lines and eleven years of naming; a category, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ category I remember is the one at the end, which was filled in 1981 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ category, my grandmother said in 1986, is the only thing that improves by being filled; every category, she said, is a kind that has agreed to look like a box. She said the kind was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 类别；种类；范畴
B. n. 类别（指那一栏本身，与条目相对）
C. 固定搭配：name a category 给一个类别命名
D. n. 类别（指表格中每一栏）
E. n. 类别（指末尾那一栏）
F. n. 种类；范畴（抽象：与那一栏相对）
G. n. 那个范畴（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a category she could not fill
The category, meaning the box and not the entries
category was the whole of the kind
the category had become a number in a report
The category of the whole thing
A category, my grandmother said in 1986

answers.why: name a category 意为“给一个类别命名”，1961 年母亲被派去给一个她填不满的类别命名。
category 意为“类别”，指那一栏本身而不是条目，共九行，由最后走的人填写。
category 指表格中每一栏类别，每一栏都是同样的表头。
category 指末尾那一栏（办事员留的那一栏），是唯一有人认真命名过的。
category 意为“种类、范畴”，与那一栏相对，父亲说 category 就是那个种类的全部。
category 为抽象用法，指那个范畴本身，是学科里人人都用、却没人质疑的东西。
category 意为“类别、种类”，到 1976 年这一栏 category 成了报告里的一个数字。
category 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九行和十一年的命名。
category 意为“类别”，我记得的是末尾那一栏，1981 年填满，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
category 为抽象总称，祖母说类别是唯一会因为被填满而变好的东西。
